source_text:
ὑποκάθηται γὰρ τὼν ἀγγέλων τὸ εὐκλεὲς ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις–, ἦν δὲ καὶ οὕτως
ὑπεράνω παντὸς ὀνόματος ὀνομαζομένου. Hebr 1,7–8 Ὥσπερ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀπαυγάσματος
καὶ τοῦ χαρακτῆρος ἐμιμήσατο τὸν νοῦν Ἰωάννου, λόγον ὀνομάσαντος καὶ πρὸς
θεὸν εἶναι εἰπόντος, οὕτως καὶ ἐνταῦθα μιμεῖται τὸν Ἰωάννην. ὥσπερ ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν·
οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ, πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, ἀντὶ τοῦ οὗτος ἦν, ταῦτα οὐκ ἦν, οὕτως
καὶ ὁ Παῦλος· πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀγγέλους· ὁ ποιῶν, πρὸς δὲ τὸν υἱόν· ὁ θρόνος σου– ἵνα
δείξῃ· τὸ μὲν ποιούμενον οὐκ ἦν, ὁ δὲ θρόνον ἔχων αἰώνιον ἀεὶ πρὸς πατέρα ἦν.
Hebr 1,12–14 Οὐ μεταβολὴν λέγει φύσεως γινομένην, ἀλλὰ κατὰ σύγκρισιν, ὅτι
ἐγχωρεῖ ταῦτα ἀπολέσθαι μᾶλλον καὶ ὥσπερ ἀπόλλυται ὅσον πρὸς παράθεσιν τῆς
τοῦ υἱοῦ ἀϊδιότητος. καὶ γὰρ ὁ κύριος προλέγων τὴν δευτέραν παρουσίαν, ἀστέρας
μὲν πεσεῖσθαι λέγει, οὐκέτι δὲ ἥλιον ἢ σελήνην ἢ οὐρανόν. Πρὸς τίνα δὲ τῶν
ἀγγέλων εἴρηκέν ποτε; ἀφεὶς τὴν κτίσιν πᾶσαν τὸ ταύτης ἀνώτερον λέγει, τοὺς
ἀγγέλους· εἰ γὰρ πρὸς ἀγγέλους διαφορὰ τῷ υἱῷ κατὰ τὸ τοὺς μὲν γενέσθαι, τὸν δὲ
μὴ γενέσθαι, πόσῳ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ ἀόρατα πάντα; δεῖ δὲ ἐπισημήνασθαι ὅτι διὰ τοῦ
σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ, καὶ τὸ προαιώνιον καὶ τὸ ἄτρεπτον τῆς φύσεως ἐδήλωσεν, καὶ διὰ
τοῦ φάναι· οὐχὶ πάντες εἰσὶ λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα εἰς διακονίαν ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι ὁ
υἱὸς οὐκ ἔστι λειτουργὸς ἀλλὰ συνεργός. 348 Hebr 2,2–3 Οὐ νόμον λέγει, ἀλλὰ τὸν
πολλάκις δι' ἀγγέλων οἰκονομηθέντα. ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη.
τοῦτο ὅμοιόν ἐστιν ἐκείνῳ τῷ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Γαλάτας ἐπιστολῇ, τῷ ἀνέβην κατὰ
ἀποκάλυψιν, καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ
ἔδραμον. ἐβεβαιώθη δὲ οὐχ ἡμῶν δεηθέντων, ἀλλὰ τῶν ἄλλων πάντων
πληροφορηθέντων, ὅτι ἃ κηρύσσω, καλῶς κηρύσσω. Hebr 2,5–9 Τὸν μέλλοντα
αἰῶνα λέγει. αὐτίκα τελευταῖον ἐπήγαγεν· νῦν δὲ οὔπω ὁρῶμεν αὐτῷ ὑποτεταγμένα
τὰ πάντα· τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρ' ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν. ὥστε τὸ τί
ἐστιν ὅτι μιμνήσκῃ αὐτοῦ; τῷ Ἰησοῦ προσήκειν φησίν· τὰ γὰρ τῆς κοινῆς
ἀνθρωπότητος αὐτῷ προσῆκεν. ἀλλὰ ὡς αὐτὸς ὁ υἱὸς λέγει τὸ ἐκ στόματος νηπίων
καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον ἕνεκεν τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου, καὶ ὄψομαι τοὺς
οὐρανοὺς ἔργα τῶν δακτύλων σου, οὐδεὶς δ' ἂν εἴποι τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὗ ἐμνήσθη ὁ
θεός, πεποιηκέναι τὸν ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων καταρτισάμενον αἶνον
ἕνεκεν τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου, καὶ ὄψομαι τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἔργα τῶν δακτύλων σου· οὗτος
ἐμνήσθη τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ ἠλάττωσεν αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρ' ἀγγέλους. τίς δὲ ὁ
ἄνθρωπος; Ἰησοῦς. διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου ἠλαττωμένος βραχύ τι παρ'
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the Hebrews 1:3 note] ... for the nature of man sits below the glory of the angels, yet he was even so above every name that is named.
Hebrews 1:7-8. Just as in the case of the radiance and the stamp he imitated the thought of John, who named (him) Word and said he was with God, so here too he imitates John. Just as that one said: "this one was in the beginning," "all things came to be through him," in place of: this one was, these things were not; so also Paul: to the angels, "who makes," but to the Son, "your throne," so that he may show: the thing made was not, but the one having an eternal throne always was with the Father.
Hebrews 1:12-14. He does not mean a change of nature happening, but (speaks) by comparison, that these things can rather perish and as it were perish, so far as concerns setting them beside the everlastingness of the Son. For indeed the Lord, foretelling the second coming, says stars will fall, but no longer sun or moon or heaven. "And to which of the angels has he ever said?" Leaving aside all creation he names what is higher than it, the angels; for if there is a difference for the Son in relation to angels, in that they came to be and he did not come to be, how much more in relation to all the invisible things? And one must note that through "but you are the same" he showed both the before-the-ages and the unchangeable of the nature, and through saying "are not all ministering spirits for service" he showed that the Son is not a minister but a co-worker.
Hebrews 2:2-3. He does not mean the law, but the (word) many times administered through angels. "It was confirmed to us by those who heard." This is like that (passage) in the letter to the Galatians: "I went up according to revelation, and laid before them the gospel, lest somehow I am running or ran in vain." And it was confirmed, not because we needed (it), but because all the others were fully convinced that what I preach, I preach well.
Hebrews 2:5-9. He means the coming age. At once, at the last, he added: "but now we do not yet see all things subjected to him; but we see Jesus made a little lower than angels." So the (words) "what is it that you remember him?" he says belong to Jesus; for the things of common humanity belonged to him. But as the Son himself says "out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you prepared praise because of your enemies," and "I will see the heavens, works of your fingers," no one would say that the man whom God remembered (is the one who) did (this), the one who prepared praise out of the mouth of infants and sucklings because of your enemies, and (said) "I will see the heavens, works of your fingers": this one remembered the man and made him a little lower than angels. And who is the man? Jesus. Through the suffering of death made a little lower than [continues in the next section: angels]
pass_b_english: … for human nature ranks below the glory of the angels, yet even so he was “far above every name that is named” (Ephesians 1:21).

On Hebrews 1:7–8: With “radiance” and “stamp” he followed John’s thought, for John called him the Word and said that he was with God. Here too he follows John. John said, “He was in the beginning” (John 1:2) and “All things came into being through him” (John 1:3), meaning: he was, and these things were not. So too Paul: to the angels, “who makes”, but to the Son, “your throne”. He wants to show that what is made once was not, while the one whose throne is eternal was always with the Father.

On Hebrews 1:12–14: He is not speaking of a change in their nature but making a comparison. These things are more liable to perish, and set beside the everlasting life of the Son they are as good as perishing. Indeed, the Lord, foretelling his second coming, says that the stars will fall (Matthew 24:29), but no longer the sun, the moon or the heaven. “To which of the angels has he ever said …?” Passing over the whole creation, he names what stands above it, the angels. For if the Son differs from the angels, in that they came into being and he did not, how much more does he differ from all the invisible things? Notice also that by saying “But you are the same”, he showed that the Son’s nature is before the ages and cannot change. And by saying “Are they not all ministering spirits sent to serve?”, he showed that the Son is not a minister but a fellow worker.

On Hebrews 2:2–3: He does not mean the law, but the word that was many times delivered through angels. “It was confirmed to us by those who heard.” This is like the passage in the letter to the Galatians: “I went up by revelation and laid before them the gospel, lest somehow I should be running, or had run, in vain” (Galatians 2:2). It was confirmed, not because we needed it, but so that all the others might be fully assured that what I preach, I preach rightly.

On Hebrews 2:5–9: He means the age to come. And straight after, at the end, he added: “But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him; but we see Jesus, made a little lower than the angels” (Hebrews 2:8–9). So the words “What is man, that you remember him?” (Hebrews 2:6), he says, belong to Jesus, since what belongs to our common humanity belonged to him. But it is the Son himself who says, “Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise because of your enemies” (Psalm 8:2) and “I will look at the heavens, the works of your fingers” (Psalm 8:3). No one would say that the man whom God remembered is the one who did this, the one who “prepared praise out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies because of your enemies” and who will “look at the heavens, the works of your fingers”. choices.why: The old English 'imitated the mind in the dawn and the character' mistook ἀπαύγασμα/χαρακτήρ (the 1:3 words) for something else.
rejected: imitated the mind in the dawn and the character (old)

choices.term: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ, πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο
choices.why: Two separate verses of John quoted together; each cited.

choices.english: He is not speaking of a change in their nature
choices.why: Refers to 'they will perish ... they will be changed' (1:11–12) said of earth and heavens.

choices.term: ἀστέρας μὲν πεσεῖσθαι λέγει, οὐκέτι δὲ ἥλιον ἢ σελήνην ἢ οὐρανόν
choices.english: the stars will fall (Matthew 24:29), but no longer the sun, the moon or the heaven
choices.why: Matthew 24:29 has the stars falling; Severian notes the sun, moon and heaven are not said to fall.

choices.term: οὐχὶ πάντες εἰσὶ λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα εἰς διακονίαν
choices.english: “Are they not all ministering spirits sent to serve?”
choices.why: SOURCE_ISSUES item 4: the old English 'are not all they are ministering spirits for service' was garbled.
rejected: are not all they are ministering spirits for service

choices.term: οὐδεὶς δ' ἂν εἴποι τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὗ ἐμνήσθη ὁ θεός, πεποιηκέναι τὸν … καταρτισάμενον αἶνον …· οὗτος ἐμνήσθη τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
choices.english: No one would say that the man whom God remembered is the one who did this … It is the Son who remembered the man
choices.why: SOURCE_ISSUES item 4. The argument: the speaker of Psalm 8 (who prepares praise and looks at the heavens he made) is the Son; the man he remembers is Jesus in his humanity. πεποιηκέναι is awkward with the participle and may be corrupt; rendered by sense ('is the one who did this') and noted. οὗτος refers back to 'the Son himself', so 'the Son' is named.
rejected: no one would say that the man of whom God remembered, having prepared praise ... had prepared it (old)
